Container.Name: Stackyard
Container.Overview: A self-hosted homelab dashboard you actually want to look at.[br][br]Most dashboards are a wall of numbers and charts. Stackyard is the opposite: a calm, launcher-style grid of app tiles, folders, and a small number of genuinely useful widgets. Built to be glanced at a hundred times a day without feeling cluttered.[br][br]Everything is set up from the browser. Add app tiles, group them into folders, arrange pages, and drop in widgets for the services you already run. Widgets cover Docker, system health, downloads, media, backups, network and more.[br][br]Runs as one container with no external database and no runtime dependencies. Configuration and uploaded icons persist in the two paths below.[br][br]Note: most homelab services live on private addresses. The Allow Private IPs setting below is on by default so links and widgets pointing at your other containers work. Turn it off to keep the SSRF guard enabled.

Container.DonateText: If Stackyard is useful to you, you can buy me a coffee.
Container.Changes:
### 1.17.0 - 2026-10-11
### Added
- Add an Update Every setting to System Summary, from 5 seconds to 1 minute.
- Point at a System Summary chart to see a past reading, or at a disk to see its used and total size.
- The logo on the About page turns its arc once on hover or tap.
- A sideways trackpad swipe or mouse wheel turns dashboard pages, one page per gesture.
### Changed
- Redesign System Summary with coloured figures in the small size and column charts in the medium size.
- Show the System Summary network line in the medium size only.
- Show System Summary temperatures in whole degrees.
- Redesign the GitHub widget with a headline figure, a cleaner pull request list and a contribution grid that fills the card.
- Point at a day on the GitHub contribution grid to see its date and count.
- The GitHub widget now follows the light and dark theme.
- Redesign the digital clock as large overlapping hour and minute figures in the analog clock's colours.
- Name a config export downloaded straight from the API `stackyard-config.json`, matching the Export button.
- The connections map places each country's dots on its most populated areas.
- Widgets render sharp on 1x screens.
### Removed
- The GitHub widget no longer offers an extra large size. Existing extra large GitHub widgets become large.
### Fixed
- About link icons keep their colours after the pointer moves over the list.
- System Summary reports a Beszel account that cannot read its systems as a sign-in problem instead of an empty hub.
- The digital clock shows its digits in the right order on a Persian dashboard.
- Remove the thin dark lines along the sides of the Now Playing widget.
- Editing an app no longer drops a summed Live Activity badge's unit, colour and minimum.
- Editing an app set up in an older version no longer drops its Live Activity headers, including a stored API key.
- Every number listed by Fetch in Live Activity now shows on the badge, including Prometheus metrics with labels, names containing dots or dashes, nested lists and plain-number answers.
- The Live Activity poll interval is now used: each service is read once per interval, however many dashboards are open.
- A badge whose service answers with an error now keeps its last value, marked out of date, instead of showing 0 or a number from the error page.
- A badge reading a response too large to read in full now reports it instead of showing a short count.
- A folder badge is now marked out of date when an app inside it fails its poll.
- TrueNAS disk health no longer names TrueNAS 26 in its unsupported-version message.
- The time since the last update, shown on a failed widget, now meets text contrast in both themes.
- A widget built from the template no longer shows its previous items under "Nothing here" when a refresh comes back empty.
- Changing a widget's display settings, such as Weather units or city, a GitHub view or a slot colour, no longer asks for its API key or password again.
- Widgets no longer stay blank when the widget list fails to load once while the dashboard starts.
- System Summary no longer shows Unraid's own error text when Unraid reports a problem.
- A widget manifest whose options are not value and label pairs is now refused at startup instead of showing "undefined" in its settings.
- Keep the warning that a stored credential must be entered again on screen after a save.
- Restore settings from a backup, not only apps, folders and widgets.
- Upgrade a backup from an older release when it is restored.
- Show a credential as missing after a restore when it was not kept.
- Keep the current wallpaper when a restored backup names an uploaded wallpaper this install does not have.
- Refuse a config whose folder contents are not a list of item ids, instead of saving it and breaking the dashboard.
- Import a link written as `host:port` from Homepage or Dashy as a working `http://` link.
- Drop a health-check address from Homepage or Dashy that only the other dashboard can resolve, instead of importing a check that always fails.
- Refuse a Homepage or Dashy file whose merge keys expand too far, instead of freezing the page.
- Read a Homepage or Dashy file with very long lines without freezing the page.
- The connections map draws users from small countries such as Belgium, Switzerland, Israel and Singapore.
- A second service in the same country no longer covers the first one's dots on the connections map.
- The connections map key no longer runs over the map with many services or long names.
- The settings navigation no longer jumps when the version number loads.
- The settings page no longer shifts sideways when its scrollbar appears.
### Security
- Changing the port map now asks for stored API keys again instead of sending them to the newly mapped host.
- Turning on Allow self-signed certificate for an app now asks for its stored API key again before it is sent without certificate checking.
- Secrets in a widget setting that is declared more than once, one per provider, are no longer sent to the browser or written to the config export.
- System Summary no longer reuses one Beszel account's login for a widget configured with a different account or password.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the dashboard is reached on.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Dashboard configuration. Keep this, or every setting is lost on update.

Config.Name: Icon Storage
Config.Description: Icons you upload for your app tiles.

Config.Name: Allow Private IPs
Config.Description: Let widgets and badges reach private addresses, which most homelab services use. Set to false to keep the SSRF guard on.

Config.Name: Docker Socket Proxy URL
Config.Description: Optional. Address of a Docker socket proxy, for the Docker widgets. Example: http://socket-proxy:2375

Config.Name: Trust Proxy
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true when running behind a reverse proxy, so client addresses are read from the forwarded headers.

Config.Name: Node Options
Config.Description: Node heap cap. Keep it near half the --memory limit in Extra Parameters, and raise both together.
